clue.text: Man in church taking Prior's pew hard to dislodge

indicators.note: dislodging the letters knocks them out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the word is used whole, its S included
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A churchgoer insists on sitting in the prior's pew and will not budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dislodge' signals an anagram of PRIORS, PEW and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper is a person attending a church service, a fair description of a man in church.

clue.text: Complaining of joint in limb

indicators.note: in means the joint is placed inside the word for limb

parts.note: a wing is a bird's limb
a hinge is a joint

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a painful joint in an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Whingeing is British slang for grumbling or moaning.

clue.text: Fighting -— poor ref gets blame

indicators.note: fighting suggests the letters are in turmoil, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a scrap, the weak referee takes the criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, an expression of blame or disapproval.

clue.text: Not late round at friend

indicators.note: round means the phrase surrounds the short word

parts.note: in time means not late

explanation.surface: A punctual pal arriving on time.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate is a close friend or confidant.

clue.text: Series of jobs as artist?

parts.note: a working life of several jobs at once, playfully read as an artist's career built on the case of drawings carried to show clients

explanation.definitionFit: A working life made up of several part-time jobs held together, named after the artist's case of work.

clue.text: Afterwards turning up to hold one sort of sale

indicators.note: to hold means the reversed word contains the numeral
in a down clue, turning up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: later means afterwards
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Later on, someone arrives to run a kind of sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses LATER to RETAL; 'to hold' puts I inside before the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is selling to the public in small quantities, as opposed to wholesale.

clue.text: Measure of insulation given by a draped cloth

parts.note: a tog is a unit measuring the warmth of duvets and clothing

explanation.surface: How warm a draped piece of fabric keeps you.
explanation.walkthrough: The tog rating is the British unit for how warm a duvet is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman toga was a single length of woollen cloth wrapped and draped around the body.

clue.text: City entrance has church and pub

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A gateway to the town boasts both a church and a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London; Temple Bar marked its western gateway.
explanation.definitionFit: Temple Bar was the ceremonial gateway into the City of London on Fleet Street.

clue.text: Northerner's extremely gruesome alternative to do?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: extremely asks for the two outermost letters of the word

parts.note: in the saying do or die, the alternative to do is the other half of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone from the north asks for a gruesome option instead of the usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives GE; the phrase do or die supplies the rest. A Geordie is a native of Tyneside, around Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Geordie is the nickname for a native of Newcastle and Tyneside in north-east England.

clue.text: As trader, I have role in Macbeth

parts.note: having a role means playing it, so 'I have role' reads as I'm, I am that character
the drunken Porter is a comic part in Shakespeare's Macbeth

explanation.surface: An actor boasts of a part in Macbeth while posing as a merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' and 'have' are link words; the Porter is the gatekeeper in Macbeth's famous knocking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a merchant who brings goods in from abroad to sell.

clue.text: One beaten in test twice coming back

indicators.note: twice asks for the piece to be written two times over
coming back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed in a test on two occasions and returning for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns MOT into TOM, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a drum, something struck with the hands or sticks.

clue.text: Sellers for example are persistent

definitions.meaning: Peter Sellers was one of the ..., from the British radio comedy The ... Show
to keep going, carry on doing something

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Sellers starred in The Goon Show; to keep at something is to carry on without stopping.

clue.text: Woman from fashionable part of London without a title

indicators.note: without means the named letter is left out of the district's name

parts.note: Mayfair is an upmarket district of central London
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A woman from smart Mayfair who has no aristocratic title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title' looks like a peerage, but it is the name of a show: the musical My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: My Fair Lady is the title of the Lerner and Loewe stage musical and film.

clue.text: Good book, one in final English edition for kids …

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the rearranged letters
a new edition reworks the material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, part of the Bible
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Bible and a final English edition published for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edition' rearranges FINAL and E into INFALE; 'in' puts NT and I inside it after INFA.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile means of or suited to infants, so for very young children.

clue.text: How daffodils appeared to Wordsworth: neat, local arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy local flower display, recalling Wordsworth's daffodils.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem: 'When all at once I saw a crowd, / A host, of golden daffodils'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem says the poet saw the golden host suddenly, in a single moment.

clue.text: … children's author is shortly back for another

indicators.note: back means the shortened name is read in reverse
shortly cuts the final letter off the author's name

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a writer for children is soon back with another book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims NESBIT to NESBI and 'back' reverses it. 'another' follows the ellipsis: another author, the Norwegian playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was a dramatist, so a further author after the children's writer in the clue.

clue.text: Tony failed to overcome right-wingers' endless bad reputation

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome is to sit over and around the other piece
failed suggests the letters have gone wrong and are reordered
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Tony failed to defeat the right wing, ending with a poor name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges TONY into NO...TY, which goes round TORIE, the TORIES minus the end, as 'endless' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, an ill reputation.

clue.text: Crushed, mischief-maker behaved unnaturally

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite
to act is to put on a show rather than be natural

explanation.surface: A naughty child, flattened, put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacted means pressed firmly together, wedged or crushed.

clue.text: Love to visit women, confined here?

indicators.note: to visit means the letter goes inside the word for women

parts.note: gals is informal for women or girls
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover calls on women who are kept shut away.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from a nil score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaols are prisons, the places where people are confined.

clue.text: Song by crow in the past a busy flier

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
crew is an old past tense of crow, as of a cockerel

explanation.surface: A tune sung by a bird long ago, one always on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the pieces side by side; the cock crew is the old past form of crowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircrew are the people who fly and work aboard an aircraft, constantly airborne.

clue.text: Bird wants part of crocus, or insect

parts.note: a crocus grows from a corm, its underground storage stem
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird wants either a bit of crocus or a bug to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a dark diving seabird that feeds on fish.

clue.text: Caribbean island, as opposed to Pacific one miles away

parts.note: anti means against, opposed to

indicators.note: miles away means the M for miles is removed

parts.note: Guam is an island in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: One island in the Caribbean, set against a far-off Pacific one.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is an island in the Lesser Antilles, part of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Book is excellent — what a surprise!

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 written as I
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A book praised as superb, to a reader's delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a prophetic book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: City kid is hot stuff

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
lava is molten rock from a volcano

explanation.surface: A child is considered very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot stuff' looks like a compliment for the kid, but it is literal molten rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Bratislava is the capital city of Slovakia.

clue.text: Endless gaze — up at this?

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to stare is to gaze

explanation.surface: A never-ending gaze at the sky, wondering what one looks at.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is what one gazes up at in the night sky.

clue.text: Country controlled by British? That's over

parts.note: to run is to control or manage

indicators.note: over means the abbreviation is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Was this country under British rule? Not any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a sultanate on Borneo, a former British protectorate.

clue.text: Magic figure mustn't start to be confusing

definitions.note: a participle standing for the verb sense, to make confused

indicators.note: mustn't start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the pentangle, a five-pointed star, is a magical symbol

explanation.surface: A magician's symbol must not begin to confuse the onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; the definition is loose, read as the act of confusing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to twist up or muddle, making a situation confusing.

clue.text: Pretty short flower for border

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: the River Tweed, a flower in the sense of something that flows, marks part of the England-Scotland border

explanation.surface: A small flower suitable for planting in a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, a thing that flows; 'border' is the Anglo-Scottish border, not a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively pretty, quaint or sentimental.

clue.text: From ancestors to present time covered in record

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: covered in means the letter sits inside the word for record

parts.note: a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: From one's forebears to the present day, all set down in a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits are passed down from one's forebears.
